transcript: Last night, Sylvia and I saw the first preview of Dead Outlaw at the Minneta Lane Theatre. This new musical is by the folks who did The Band's Visit, which I absolutely loved, so this was very highly anticipated for me. Director David Cromer gave a little pre-show speech with the disclaimer that there might be some hiccups they'd need to stop and address since this was the first preview. But it seemed pretty smooth sailing from our point of view. To cut to the chase, the score definitely lived up to my expectations. I didn't really know what to expect stylistically, nor did I know anything about the plot, and to me the surprise was definitely part of the fun here. But if you are curious and you wanna keep listening, this musical tells the true story of a man named Elmer McCurdy, who experienced many adventures and went many places both before and after his death. He is the titular character, the Dead Outlaw, and is played wonderfully by Andrew Durand, who you may have recently seen in Shucked. The music is mostly folky-rock-grassroots kind of vibes, and the band is on stage the entire time which is pretty cool. The plot is very out there, and structurally this musical is quite subversive, but to me the music is the core of the project and the thing that really provides momentum and keeps you engaged. The songwriting is just lovely and is definitely something I would love to have a cast recording of. Dead Outlaw is currently running through early April, and definitely has my recommendation. I'm really curious to see how it changes throughout previews and what others come to think of it. With that, another playbill for my collection.
